title: Oxygen change at fixed density accounts for 72% of the P02 oxygen stock loss in density 26.3-26.7 at 180-150 W, 2004-2022
abstract: We tested whether oxygen loss on one North Pacific density surface also represents loss across a layer with finite mass. We used four CCHDO bottle files from P02 in 2004, 2013 and 2022, matched in longitude at 28-32 N. We split oxygen stock change exactly into oxygen change at fixed density and mass redistribution, summed over 0.01 kg/m3 density slices. At 180-150 W, stock in sigma0 26.3-26.7 fell by 2.82 mol/m2, or 9.1%, from 2004 to 2022. The conditional 95% spatial block interval is -3.32 to -2.37. The fixed-density term was -2.02 mol/m2 and accounts for 72% of the loss (conditional share interval 58-83%). Mass change accounts for -0.80. Bottle salinity, three-degree bins, two other density bands and a half-size density step retain the central loss. The fixed-density loss remains negative under an assumed independent 1% oxygen scale-error envelope. In the east, mass gain offsets about 48% of the endpoint fixed-density loss. Most of the sampled western stock rebound after 2013 comes from mass gain. Strict interpolation leaves too few central casts, and cruise seasons differ. The result gives a finite-layer target for outcrop models. It does not assign the loss to ventilation or respiration, establish an eastward speed, or estimate a basin inventory. Code, source hashes, aggregate results, checks and a figure are included; raw records stay external.

display.caption: Oxygen stock changes in the sigma0 26.3-26.7 layer on P02 at 28-32 N. Black: total. Blue: fixed-density concentration term. Orange: mass term. Bars: conditional 95% spatial block intervals. Regional coverage differs; the western range is incomplete.
